attack_mechanism: Probing `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]` in this early-round window exposes an internal representation before all 24 rounds have diffused the input. On the first calculation step after `accept`, the padded rate block has just been XORed into the persistent state and is being evaluated by the two-round Keccak network. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]` is the unpacked 64-bit input lane used by theta; its bits are deterministic functions of the newly accepted `keccak_in` block and the previous state. The effect traverses `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.padder_out_1 -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]`. The observation leaks lane-level information about the secret input that is not present as a directly accessible architectural signal.

Sampling `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]` at a fixed cycle offset across repeated operations supplies aligned intermediate values for differential or correlation analysis. On subsequent `calc` cycles, feedback from the registered permutation output re-enters the same combinational round network. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]` is recomputed for later round pairs and therefore yields a time series of input-dependent values from the unpacked 64-bit input lane used by theta. The effect traverses `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.padder_out_1 -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_in -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[3][1]`. Combining those observations can recover secret-dependent relationships even when a single lane observation is insufficient to reconstruct the input.
